tour.title: An accepted turn keeps running
tour.say: Web and phone clients ask accepted turns to continue after a disconnect, so changing pages or losing the network does not silently press Stop.

tour.title: Know the real state
tour.say: The server publishes whether a turn is running, completed, stopped or failed, with a reason, so reconnecting clients do not infer activity from an empty bubble.

tour.title: Recover steps and the reply

tour.title: Stop stays explicit
tour.say: Stop ends the turn, and watchdogs still bound stalled work. After a backend restart, a turn without a reply is shown as interrupted.

tour.title: Keep drafts and conversation context
tour.say: Each conversation keeps its own draft, chosen personality and history. Returning to a thread restores its text without moving another thread’s draft.

tour.title: See which chats are working

tour.title: Reuse the turn screenshot
tour.say: When its route can take images, the action rail attaches the turn’s screenshot. It goes only once: after the next action it may show a screen that is gone, so later steps decide from text.

tour.title: Scale it to fit
tour.say: Real captures are often too big. A Retina browser page can be more than four thousand pixels wide, so the host scales it down to the model’s limit instead of dropping it.

tour.title: Chat sees it too
tour.say: Chat’s rail does the same with the newest tool result’s image, never with one from an earlier call, because a click may have changed the screen since.

tour.title: Validate before dispatch
tour.say: Each referenced image must be a PNG or JPEG within the declared dimensions and byte limit. The engine refuses anything else rather than resizing it.

tour.title: Respect capability and locality
tour.say: Image requests skip text-only models. Local processing still excludes remote body-seeing routes, and token fit accounts for each image use.

tour.title: The planner keeps the picture
tour.say: The agent’s planner model keeps the newest screenshot for up to three more steps, captioned with what ran since, so it never has to hunt for an image it already took.

tour.title: Plan mode begins

tour.title: A pipeline of specialists

tour.title: Rules pick each stage
tour.say: After every stage, ordered code rules read which artifacts exist and choose the next agent, pause for a question, or finish. No model is asked to steer the pipeline.

tour.title: Understand the request
tour.say: The analyzer decides whether the message is a new task, an answer to a pending question, or a status check, and rates its clarity and complexity, using decision engine answers before a model call.

tour.title: Pull out the details

tour.title: Choose a strategy
tour.say: Without spending a model call, the selector picks atomic composition by default, and guided search for complex multi-step work, keeping search parameters ready as a fallback.

tour.title: Compose the steps
tour.say: A reasoning model first drafts an outline of goals, then expands it into concrete tool steps from the permitted catalog, retrying with corrective feedback when the draft does not hold together.

tour.title: Check the plan
tour.say: The planner adds dependencies, success criteria and where each parameter came from, rejects any cycle, and validates the plan contract before saving it for you to approve.

features.name: Answers backed by evidence
features.oneLine: Check final answers against available evidence, keep the answer readable, and open an info icon to see the saved verification reason.
features.maturityEvidence: FilesystemTaskUserFinalizer synthesizes then calls verify_task_user_answer on every task answer (magician/src/magician_v2/artifact_v2/service.rs:48809,48834); chat replies are checked through checked_chat_reply (magician/src/magician_v2/chat/service.rs:17075); the agentic loop reviews its terminal draft with the same core (magician/src/magician_v2/execution/agentic/executor.rs:25053); notify_owner and Relentless reports call check_owner_text (execution/compiled_handlers/notify_owner.rs:52, relentless_service.rs:1874); operations v3_task_user_output_synthesis and evidence_precision_judge mapped in llm-router.yaml:4772,4702.

Agent's final draft reviewed per claim
Read a total with its context
Keep runtime status out of the answer

uiSurface.description: Chat messages and task Run panels on Web, iPhone and Android show verification status through an info control. The popup shows the saved reason immediately; headings, paragraphs and the answer body remain in the message.

tour.title: The run finishes
tour.say: When a task's run ends, the finalizer builds an evidence bundle, has a model write the answer, and checks it before anything is published to you.

tour.title: Gather the evidence
tour.say: The answer draws on the whole run, including delegated results, recorded file changes and Magician’s own records, with real tool evidence ahead of call noise.

tour.title: Write the answer
tour.say: The synthesis model may compress and format the evidence, but a fixed policy forbids it from strengthening claims, adding advice, or reporting a failure that a later success already closed.

tour.title: Know each source
tour.say: Every piece of evidence is labelled by origin. A tool result can prove a claim, but text the agent wrote itself can never prove a figure on its own.

tour.title: Split into claims
tour.say: The answer is broken into sentences, list items, table rows and code blocks, and every figure is located in the evidence by code, across lakh, crore, million and percentage formats.

tour.title: Judge each claim
tour.say: A judge model rules on each claim with its own evidence. A failing core claim fails the answer, while unsupported side remarks are removed and recorded beside the answer.

tour.title: One bounded repair
tour.say: If a core claim fails, the synthesizer gets one chance to remove or qualify it, and the repaired answer is checked again from scratch.

tour.title: Honest when unsure
tour.say: When checks cannot confirm every claim, the answer stays readable and its verification note keeps the specific reason available from an info control.

tour.title: Verification in task detail
tour.say: The iPhone task Run panel uses the same compact verification treatment as chat, keeping the reason in a popup beside a formatted answer.

tour.title: Readable on Android too
tour.say: Android shares the verification popup between chat and task detail, with separate headings, paragraphs and lists instead of showing the full answer as a warning.

tour.title: Read a total with its context
tour.say: A reported total is checked with surrounding facts and item records, so matching a number alone cannot prove the claim.

tour.title: Keep runtime status out of the answer
tour.say: Usable prose can be recovered from a rejected model response. Internal completed-and-blocked status lists stay separate from the answer built from evidence.

tour.title: Run events become widgets
tour.say: A background emitter listens to every agent run. A start becomes an empty progress gauge, each iteration fills it, and each decision or action adds a line to a live agent log.

tour.title: Calm the stream
tour.say: Gauge updates for the same component within two hundred milliseconds collapse into the latest one, while every log line passes straight through, because no line of the log may be lost.

tour.title: Save, then broadcast
tour.say: Each batch is applied to the agent's layout document and saved in its scope before it goes out as a UI delta event, so the screen survives a restart.

tour.title: Late joiners catch up
tour.say: A screen that opens mid-run asks over the websocket for a snapshot, served from the emitter's shared cache first and disk second, then follows the live deltas.

tour.title: Bind data to widgets
tour.say: Components can carry a JSON path query over their data, and the server resolves it into a static snapshot so every client draws the same rows.

tour.title: Results become screens
tour.say: When a finished task asks to publish a surface, its output is turned into the same document type, with metric grids, tables and a download link, instead of a bare file.

tour.title: Only known widgets
tour.say: Every document is validated before it is stored: version one, unique ids, a fixed component vocabulary, depth and size limits, and bounded graphs, so a model can never ship arbitrary markup.

tour.title: Pack from the CLI
tour.say: A developer scaffolds, checks, tests and packs an app with the magician app command, which reuses the same strict package admission the server applies.

tour.title: Find building blocks
tour.say: Authoring looks up tools, agents and procedures in one primitive catalog, where every entry carries exact identities and digests rather than just friendly names.

tour.title: Compile the recipes
tour.say: Each workflow recipe is treated as hostile input and compiled into a validated, versioned form; compiling grants no authority and does not make a recipe ready.

tour.title: Lock dependencies
tour.say: Every declared dependency is resolved exactly once into an immutable lock, and any failure returns no partially usable lock at all.

tour.title: Publish for review
tour.say: SDK, CLI and VibeDev packages all rerun conformance, resolve the lock, and land as an inert ready-for-review installation with no grant, schedule or approval.

tour.title: Commit to the registry
tour.say: The registry writes the package revision, the conformance attempt and the reviewable installation in one transaction, inside that owner's own encrypted database.

tour.title: Diff the permissions
tour.say: An update is compared with the current grant axis by axis; expanding authority such as network destinations or background execution sends it back for owner review.

tour.title: Switch or roll back
tour.say: The new version is staged side by side and switched in one compare-and-swap; a code-only rollback restores the previous package while keeping every record written since.

features.name: App Data and Records

uiSurface.description: Per-app data cleanup panel on the Apps page

tour.title: Typed records
tour.say: Each app keeps typed records with provenance and a revision number; the records describe state but never grant authority on their own.

tour.title: Authority checked late
tour.say: Right before a tool runs, current authority is re-resolved and the tool and every context read are checked against it, so a stale grant cannot slip through.

tour.title: Bounded reads
tour.say: Queries run against a server-held snapshot with strict bounds, and only opaque cursor references ever leave the service.

tour.title: All-or-nothing writes
tour.say: A write is applied as one all-or-nothing command inside the same current-authority check, and it leaves an immutable receipt that can be verified later.

tour.title: Plan the forget
tour.say: Forgetting a record first plans every cascade and nullify effect and refuses blocked links, so the owner approves exactly what will be erased.

tour.title: Erase for real
tour.say: The commit repeats that exact plan inside its transaction, uses secure delete, and leaves a receipt that can be replayed.

tour.title: Propose to memory
tour.say: When a workflow wants something remembered, it can only queue a bounded, source-linked proposal in an outbox; memory itself stays owned by its destination.

tour.title: Owner signs off
tour.say: The owner's accept, reject or revoke decision arrives as a desktop-signed envelope that embeds the exact proposal shown, and its signature is verified before it counts.

tour.title: Find due work
tour.say: Each tick the scheduler reconciles a scope's current grants and claims a small batch of due fires; a paused scope claims nothing, and missed intervals collapse into one fire.

tour.title: Recheck before launch
tour.say: Just before launch it reopens the exact durable lease, so a paused scope, a reclaimed lease or a swapped invocation cannot start a run.

tour.title: Admit under budget
tour.say: The run passes one process-wide scheduler and the installation's period budget before its root is written to the resource journal.

tour.title: Reserve, then spend
tour.say: Each consequential step reserves a conservative maximum before it touches the outside world, then settles the exact usage and releases the rest.

tour.title: Replay the ledger
tour.say: The append-only journal is the authority: replaying it under current limits yields committed usage, open reservations and any budget breaches.

tour.title: React to events
tour.say: Event behaviours fire only from the persisted record of a finished task, keyed by its source event, so replaying the same event changes nothing.

tour.title: Notify the owner
tour.say: A workflow can send the owner a one-way notification; a worker turns each queued row into an ordinary user request, and the app never sees a reply.

tour.title: Settle and reschedule
tour.say: When the run settles the schedule advances from the acceptance boundary, and a crash before settlement reuses the same idempotency key instead of firing twice.

tour.say: An app asks for one class of device action on a reviewed target; requests that would run in the background or transfer data are refused at admission.

tour.title: Owner grants it
tour.say: The owner's review turns that request into a grant bound to the locked dependency's exact digests, and it never gains an implicit all-actions meaning.

tour.title: Pair the Mac
tour.say: Pairing a Mac starts from the desktop's attested identity and the requested target apps, and the pairing moves through pending and approved before it is ever active.

tour.title: Activate the pairing

tour.title: Lower a Mac action
tour.say: A reviewed action is lowered into one closed server-to-desktop action and signed with the pairing key, so raw process and window details stay private to the server.

tour.title: Closed wire actions
tour.say: The desktop accepts only a fixed menu of actions such as launch, focus, click and type, each under a short-lived, one-shot keyed signature.

tour.title: Typed phone actions

tour.title: Open an app page
tour.say: Opening an app page sends only the route; the server works from your signed-in scope, so the browser never names which data it may see.

tour.title: Verify, then query
tour.say: Hydration loads the app's active compiled surfaces, checks their digest, matches the route, and derives one bounded query from compiler metadata, refusing if a revision changed mid-read.

tour.title: Scripts get a worker
tour.say: When an app screen ships its own script, the runtime refuses WebAssembly and starts a dedicated worker process, waiting for it to report ready before the session goes live.

tour.title: Seal the bytes
tour.say: Only the admitted surface files are copied into a private sealed folder, and the worker starts as an isolated child with no network and writes only inside that folder.

tour.title: Run the script
tour.say: Inside the child, the app script runs in an embedded JavaScript engine that offers just three calls: render, log and the bridge back to Magician.

tour.title: Kill on overrun
tour.say: The worker is polled against CPU, memory and wall-clock budgets and killed the moment it exceeds one, so a runaway screen cannot hog the machine.

tour.title: Browser-side sandbox
tour.say: The newer host path runs reviewed scripts in a browser frame allowed only to run scripts, under a kernel-made content policy that forbids any network connection.

tour.title: Gate every message
tour.say: Each bridge message must be one of eight public operations, inside message and payload watchdogs, against the live package, surface and grant revisions; anything else ends the session.

uiSurface.description: Installation review lists what each app is granted

tour.title: Know the caller
tour.say: Every app request starts from an authenticated scope recording how the caller proved itself, such as a signed-in session, a task execution or a reviewed background launch; an app body cannot forge one.

tour.title: Intersect the grants
tour.say: Authority resolution refuses system workers, disabled installations and revoked or stale grants, then intersects the owner's grant with agent, trust and parent ceilings, so each layer can only narrow it.

tour.title: Check data handling
tour.say: Before a model or external tool sees app data, the handling policy decides: some data may only reach a local model, and external hosts must be on the approved list.

tour.title: Mint a one-shot permit
tour.say: A tool call gets a permit only if the authority digest still matches, the tool is granted and every network destination is allowed; the permit is bound to one execution and one invocation.

tour.title: Run skills in place
tour.say: Skills that cannot be copied run in place inside an exec-roots jail derived from the package; if the skill or its runtime changed since approval, the run is refused until re-approval.

tour.title: Label the result
tour.say: The returned bytes are labeled under the permit, and the permit is consumed in the process, so it can never be replayed for a second result.

tour.title: Browser, tightly scoped
tour.say: Apps never get the raw browser tool; they get an isolated session owned by the installation and run, with a small closed action set and opaque element identities.

tour.title: Compose across apps
tour.say: When a personal agent moves one app's result into another app's action, the broker rechecks both grants, schemas and policies and refuses incompatible fields; apps never reach each other directly.

tour.title: Export without hostages
tour.say: Export needs only your signed-in user scope, not live app authority, so a disabled or quarantined app cannot hold your data hostage; grants, credentials, schedules and memory stay out.

tour.title: Portable references
tour.say: Links between records are rewritten to portable aliases, so source scope, record, actor and execution identities never cross into the archive.

tour.title: Preview the import
tour.say: Importing into another installation first builds a server preview; each new identity is derived from destination, archive and alias, and collisions are shown for review instead of merged.

tour.title: Commit what was reviewed
tour.say: Only the exact preview under its single approval is committed, and the import receipt and projection events are written in the same transaction as the records.

tour.title: Preview a purge
tour.say: Purging a retained installation starts with a stored preview that refuses to run while memory or retrieval retractions, or lifecycle deliveries, are still pending.

tour.title: Delete in one go
tour.say: On commit, the installation's scoped rows are deleted and checked against the preview, with the receipt and the lifecycle change saved in the same registry transaction.

tour.title: An honest receipt
tour.say: The receipt records each target as deleted, erased or retained, so shared packages, artifact evidence and audit tombstones are disclosed as kept rather than claimed as gone.

tour.title: Prove a migration
tour.say: Moving the first-party Town Square corpus into its app store uses content-derived record ids and compares counts and digests read back per table, so a re-run cannot double rows.

tour.title: Propose, never write
tour.say: A reviewed app workflow can propose a memory from records it just changed; the candidate cites its exact source records and never writes canonical memory itself.

tour.title: Owner decides
tour.say: The candidate waits as proposed until the owner accepts or rejects it; later it can be marked stale or tombstoned, each change saved against the current scope.

tour.title: Follow the source
tour.say: When an app record changes, the same transaction settles every candidate that cites it, so a memory cannot outlive the fact it came from.

tour.title: Fence before use
tour.say: Before use, eligibility is resolved again: the candidate must be accepted and its current sources must still match, otherwise it fails closed.

tour.title: Enter the prompt
tour.say: Prompt assembly re-reads the app store for eligible candidates; if the store or a source is unavailable, app memory is dropped without starving ordinary memory.

tour.title: Journal retrieval notes
tour.say: Retrieval notes for the personal agent are appended to an ordered journal inside the transaction that produced them, so the record and its note commit together or not at all.

tour.title: Deliver in order
tour.say: A worker drains one journal row at a time to the private retrieval store, so a retry after a lost response cannot fork the chain.

tour.title: Retract on removal
tour.say: When an installation is taken out of service, invalidations are appended for its live projections, and a later purge waits until those retractions are acknowledged.

tour.say: On macOS the runtime turns a one-time nonce into a Keychain identity challenge and pins only a verified Ed25519 desktop identity; an ordinary web caller is never the owner.

tour.title: Owner starts enrollment

tour.title: Phone redeems it

tour.title: Prove the handset
tour.say: The verifier checks that a hardware-backed Android Keystore key signed the exact enrollment for the reviewed Magdroid package, and keeps only a small pinned identity, not certificate bytes.

tour.title: Propose one change

tour.title: Apply in order
tour.say: The server accepts a receipt only under the pinned desktop identity, as the next generation chained to the previous digest, so forged or out-of-order approvals are refused.

tour.say: Only a configured number of trusted turns run at once, four by default. A turn beyond that waits in line and reports that it is queued.

tour.title: Every turn commits

tour.title: A sandbox copy
tour.say: For a project that is not trusted, the engine works in a shadow copy of the repo, synced from the real one before each turn, while the real repo stays read-only to it.

tour.title: Work becomes a diff
tour.say: When the turn ends, whichever engine ran it, Magician diffs the shadow copy against the real repo and stores the result as a proposal waiting for approval.

tour.title: The owner decides
tour.say: The proposal shows up as a diff to review. The owner applies all of it, picks some files, or rejects it, and a proposal that changed after review is refused.

tour.title: Apply with a net
tour.say: Before writing, the current contents of every affected file are snapshotted. If any file fails to apply, the snapshot is restored, so the repo is never left half-changed.

tour.title: Checkpoints on green
tour.say: Once an applied change passes the project's checks, a checkpoint is minted with a saved commit of the real tree, so every checkpoint is a known-good state.

tour.title: Rewind to good
tour.say: Rewinding first saves an undo point, restores the repo to the checkpoint's commit, and queues the engine session from that moment, so the agent continues from where the code now is.

tour.title: Priced from rates
tour.say: Cost is computed from the effective-dated pricing table and stamped with a pricing version, so historical costs stay auditable after rates change.

tour.title: Validated revisions
tour.say: Every record is an immutable, content-free revision keyed by kind, stable id and revision number, and it is validated before it is accepted.

tour.title: Never blocks calls
tour.say: The request path only tries a non-blocking enqueue into bounded lanes. If a lane is full, a counted gap is recorded rather than slowing the model call.

tour.title: Journal first
tour.say: A dedicated worker appends records to an fsynced journal, materializes the uncommitted prefix, and only then moves the watermark, so replay after a crash is safe.

tour.title: Deterministic Parquet
tour.say: Each revision becomes one deterministically named Parquet object in a daily partition, and duplicate delivery is checked against the existing file instead of writing twice.

tour.title: One governed reader
tour.say: A shared read service answers the LLM page and internal tools alike, assembling a trace's calls and provider attempts within the caller's scope.

tour.title: Compact settled trace files
tour.say: Older trace partitions are compacted and verified before their covered raw parts are pruned. Governed readers retain the compact plus any late-arriving tail.

features.name: Evals that check growth

tour.title: Makefile is the list
tour.say: Eval lanes are read from annotations above each Makefile target, so there is no second list to drift, and a malformed annotation shows up as an error instead of disappearing.

tour.title: Compare model and thinking
tour.say: Lifecycle evaluations compare up to three model and thinking combinations. An unavailable choice needs replacement; leaving comparisons empty uses configured routing.

tour.title: Press Run

tour.title: Refuse unsafe starts
tour.say: The runner refuses a lane already running and one whose services are not confirmed up, because a half-finished run still burns model time and money.

tour.title: An ordinary execution
tour.say: The lane runs as an internal execution that shells one make target, so cancel, progress, approvals and spend limits come for free.

tour.title: Always recorded
tour.say: The run record is written when it is dropped, so an error, a panic or a cancelled task still leaves exactly one terminal entry in the append-only history.

tour.title: Honest cost
tour.say: Cost is joined from the LLM ledger at read time. If the ledger cannot answer, the run shows unknown rather than free.

tour.title: Memory checks
tour.say: When enabled, a periodic runner renders memory exactly as agents see it, checks expected facts appear, and records pass or fail rows for the memory dashboard.

tour.title: Growth scorecard

tour.title: One edit request
tour.say: An agent asks for one edit, like trim, speed up or burn in a caption. An unknown operation or a stray parameter is refused with the right schema, so the agent can fix its call.

tour.title: Ten ready operations
tour.say: Ten operations live in one registry. Each one turns its parameters into an ffmpeg command, from trimming and converting to joining clips or turning a still image into a video.

tour.title: Stays in the workspace
tour.say: Input files are resolved inside the caller's own workspace, and the output gets a fresh file named after the operation, so an edit never reaches files it should not.

tour.title: A background job
tour.say: The edit runs as a background job, at most two at a time and capped at thirty minutes. Progress is read straight from ffmpeg while it works.

tour.title: Checking on it
tour.say: The agent polls the job until it reports completed or failed. Jobs are kept in memory, so a restart forgets them and says so plainly.

tour.title: Give it a purpose
tour.say: You start a watch from the Observe page with a purpose and, if you like, something to watch for. Only one watch of this computer runs at a time.

tour.title: A steady loop
tour.say: Every few seconds the session takes a still of the screen. It stops on its own at the time limit, after long idle stretches, or if capture keeps failing.

tour.title: Skip what didn't change
tour.say: Each still shrinks to a tiny fingerprint. If the screen barely moved, no model is called and the frame is thrown away, which keeps cost and privacy in check.

tour.title: Narrating the change
tour.say: A changed frame goes to a vision model along with your purpose and recent notes. It answers nothing, a note, or an alert, and a watch can stop itself when its condition matches.

tour.title: Listening too
tour.say: If audio is on, speech is transcribed into the same session. Only a phrase addressed to the assistant prompts a fresh look at the screen, so background chatter is never tied to it.

tour.title: A summary to keep
tour.say: When the watch ends, a summary is posted to the session and one short entry lands in your screen observations memory. The frames themselves are never kept.

tour.title: Engines from config
tour.say: At startup, the transcription engines named in the config are built into an ordered chain. When the Mac's own speech recognition is available, boot puts it first and keeps these as fallbacks.

tour.title: Resolving a surface
tour.say: When dictation or a meeting starts, its profile plus your preferences resolve to one exact engine list for each stage.

tour.title: Building the pipeline
tour.say: That profile becomes a live pipeline: streaming transcription with fallbacks, speaker labels when needed, and a voice activity gate in front.

tour.title: Only speech passes
tour.say: The gate lets only speech through, with a short lead-in so first words are not clipped. Silence never reaches the transcriber, and each utterance gets its own session.

tour.title: Your choice in Settings
tour.say: In Settings you add, remove and reorder engines for each stage, and start or unload local models.

tour.title: Saved safely
tour.say: Each change is written back to the config file only if nobody else changed it first, so two editors never silently overwrite each other.

features.name: What we told whom
features.oneLine: Records what you told whom, puts claims from conversations up for review, and finds every message a correction touches.

tour.title: Bring in a conversation
tour.say: The owner brings in a conversation, like a call typed up afterwards. This is the one route allowed to ingest a transcript.

tour.title: Act first, claims after
tour.say: The conversation is always recorded as one outward act. Every line our side said becomes a pending claim; anything it can't attribute to us is skipped with a reason.

tour.title: A person confirms
tour.say: Only a named person can confirm a claim, and never the one who extracted it, so the machine can't mark its own homework.

tour.title: Who heard what
tour.say: A confirmed claim writes one row for each act, claim and audience. That is the record of exactly what we told whom.

tour.title: Corrections find everyone
tour.say: When a figure turns out wrong, a correction looks up every active disclosure that carried it and opens an obligation to tell each audience.

tour.title: Receipts for apps
tour.say: Decisions finished through the claims review app are read off a completion journal in order and turned into review receipts, so none are lost.

features.name: Memory that tidies itself

uiSurface.description: The Memory page's observability dashboard shows temperature tiers, hot projections and memory eval runs; each crew member's workspace shows its consolidation health.

tour.title: After a run ends
tour.say: When an agent's run finishes, its episode is handed to the consolidator in the background. Paused runs are skipped, and each cycle-completed rule in the agent's definition gets a chance to update memory.

tour.title: Structured tier updates
tour.say: Structured rules need no model: the tier interpreter writes task progress, strategy records and archive summaries straight into the agent's typed memory tiers.

tour.title: A five-minute sweep
tour.say: Every five minutes a background sweep visits each agent, replays any orphaned clarification answers, runs due batch rules, then runs retention. A disabled agent with nothing pending is skipped until a revisit window passes.

tour.title: Grade episodes first
tour.say: Before a batch is merged, a model grades which episodes are worth remembering. Grades are cached durably, so a restart does not pay for the same judgement twice.

tour.title: Distil before deleting
tour.say: Episodes past their retention window are found, and when the policy asks for it they are consolidated first, so old runs leave their lessons behind before they are deleted.

tour.title: Reconcile owner claims
tour.say: A bounded reviewer, at most six per hour, compares a new claim with existing ones and labels it duplicate, reinforce, coexist, supersede, or a concrete question for the owner.

tour.title: Judge what helped
tour.say: Memories injected into a run are queued, then a batch reviewer labels each as load-bearing, useful, irrelevant, stale or harmful, and promotes winners into hot projections.

tour.title: Hot, warm, cold
tour.say: Maintenance ranks memories inside each lane and caps how many may be hot, active or warm, so the prompt keeps the memories that earn their place.

tour.title: Bounded, never deleted
tour.say: The owner's memory file has size bounds. Activity logs move to their own files, repeated notes are stored once, and anything that leaves is archived first, so every record can be restored.

tour.title: Fold repeated preferences
tour.say: Repeated preferences are folded within bounded memory lanes, with removed copies archived. Conflicts and different wording still go through the memory review rules.

features.name: Agents that wake themselves
