Agent CRUD, trigger, pause/resume, /triggers and /approvals routes are mounted at main.rs:12189-12314, and the Triggers page reads /triggers. Declaring schedules is documented in docs/components/magician/autonomous-agents.md.

locations.why: Turns a due fire into run
Cross-process file locks for agent data

uiSurface.description: The Triggers page lists each agent's schedules and recent fires; agents themselves are managed from the crew pages.

tour.title: Agents are definitions
tour.say: An agent starts life as a versioned definition on disk. Creation must be version one, and every later update must name the version it read, so two editors cannot silently overwrite each other.

tour.title: Register a schedule
tour.say: Each agent goal gets one durable scheduler entry holding its cron, event or idle trigger, its last fire time and a trigger sequence number, all saved under a cross-process lock.

tour.title: Five-second tick
tour.say: Every five seconds the supervisor walks a batch of workspaces, collects cron fires that are due, and dispatches them within a budget; fires over budget are requeued, never dropped.

tour.title: Cron in your timezone
tour.say: The next fire time is computed from a five-field cron expression in the entry's own timezone, falling back to UTC when the timezone is invalid, and impossible schedules simply never fire.

tour.title: Build the brief
tour.say: Before launch, the prompt pipeline pulls the goal, memory tiers, recent episodes and last cycle's feedback into named sections, failing fast when a required source is missing and trimming to the token budget.

tour.title: Durable wake-ups
tour.say: Retries, delegated child completions and schedule recovery wait in a persisted wake-up queue. Each due row is leased before its handler starts, so a crash cannot lose a timer.

tour.title: Resume on wake
tour.say: When a scheduled wake comes due, the runtime finds the agent and goal behind it and resumes that cycle in the right workspace.

tour.title: Ask before acting
tour.say: If a run pauses for confirmation, the approval service creates one deduplicated request and fans it out; a sweep every thirty seconds expires requests nobody answers.

features.name: Big inputs, small models
features.oneLine: Splits memory jobs too big for a local model's window into checked chunks and merges the answers back into one result.
features.maturityEvidence: Chunk adapters are registered at boot. Catalog assignments own per-operation chunking, physical model limits and same-provider recovery; the immutable activation manifest is interpreted only by the bounded offline comparison reader. See docs/components/magician/ollama-logical-context-chunking.md.

locations.why: Chunk-enabled workload assignments name their adapter

tour.title: Adapters at boot
tour.say: At startup the server registers six domain adapters: episode quality, memory utility, entities, environment, evidence distillation and memory archive. Each knows how to split and rejoin its own kind of input.

tour.title: A chunkable call
tour.say: A memory job supplies its logical input. A chunk-enabled workload assignment selects the checked chunk runner; other assignments use the normal single request.

tour.title: Will it fit
tour.say: Every physical request is estimated first: input plus reserved output plus a safety margin must fit the model's window, or the call fails before it ever reaches the provider.

tour.title: Plan the chunks
tour.say: The planner asks the adapter for logical items, splits oversized ones semantically, and packs them into chunks that keep each source's root identity and order.

tour.title: Map each chunk
tour.say: The runner sends one bounded request per chunk to the local model and validates every answer against the adapter's schema, recording telemetry as child calls of one logical call.

tour.title: Repair or fall back
tour.say: An invalid chunk answer gets a bounded repair request on the same provider, then a deterministic fallback, so one bad chunk does not sink the whole job.

tour.title: Reduce to one answer
tour.say: Validated chunk answers are reduced back into a single response, which must pass the adapter's final check before the caller ever sees it.

tour.title: Archive in checkpoints
tour.say: For long episode archives, the consolidator saves the exact grouping plan before its first write and commits one group at a time, so an interrupted job resumes where it stopped.

features.name: Taste learned from sessions
features.oneLine: Spots standing preferences in finished chats and runs, proposes them, and adds them to your taste note only once you approve.
features.maturityEvidence: The seed config turns capture on (memory.taste_profile.capture_enabled: true, magician-config.yaml:513), and the distiller is bound (llm.router.operation_mapping.taste_profile_distill, llm-router.yaml:4482). The service is installed at boot when capture is on (magician-bin/src/main.rs:10236-10248), and one TasteCaptureWorker is spawned (main.rs:11500). Review routes are mounted (main.rs:13524-13545), and TasteProposalsPanel renders on the Memory page (ui/unified-ui/src/routes/(app)/memory/+page.svelte:1235). Docs: docs/components/magician/taste-profile.md.

locations.why: JSONL store is the machine state

uiSurface.description: A taste proposals panel on the Memory page lists each pending directive with its evidence and lets the owner approve or reject it.

tour.title: Sweep finished sessions
tour.say: One background worker re-reads the list of workspaces each pass and collects transcripts from chats that went idle and runs that finished, past a saved watermark.

tour.title: Distil within a cap
tour.say: A distiller model reads each transcript for standing direction. The daily proposal cap is checked before the model call, so a capped day costs nothing.

tour.title: Admit only confident
tour.say: The reply is parsed strictly: candidates below the confidence floor are dropped, and a malformed reply is kept apart from a genuinely empty one so the session is retried.

tour.title: Proposals stay structured
tour.say: Admitted candidates are filed as JSON lines. The readable proposals note is only a mirror and is never parsed, which closes a prompt-injection path from quoted web content.

tour.title: Owner decides
tour.say: On the Memory page the owner sees each proposed directive with its evidence and approves or rejects it.

tour.title: Written into the note
tour.say: Approval appends the directive under its heading in the taste note, or removes it for a retraction, then marks the proposal approved. Replayed approvals cannot undo a later decision.

tour.title: Shapes every prompt
tour.say: The taste note is injected into chat and agent prompts as written and is never truncated, because a directive cut mid-sentence could invert its meaning.

tour.title: Checked before acting
tour.say: Preference alignment reads each note line as a taste intention. Lines the owner approved count as confirmed; anything else only advises.

features.name: Durable agent runs
features.oneLine: Agent runs survive crashes and restarts, never re-send a message blindly, and take your redirects mid-run.
features.maturityEvidence: The stateless driver is the default: an unset, blank or unknown MAGICIAN_EXECUTION_DRIVER selects it, and only 'inprocess' picks the rollback arm (run_loop/mod.rs:69-75, 165-175, 250). Boot spawns the terminal outbox projector and a 30-minute parked-run reconciler (magician-bin/src/main.rs:9339-9397, 9472-9497). POST /executions/{id}/steer is mounted at main.rs:12470 and called from ui/unified-ui/src/lib/magician/execution/controlClient.ts:86. The generic WorkerRunner is a scheduler primitive with no production caller; restart recovery re-enters the ordinary executor instead (run_loop/mod.rs:83-89).

uiSurface.description: Run controls (pause, resume, steer, cancel) used by the live runs strip and command palette

tour.title: Pick the durable driver
tour.say: Each run picks its driver once. Unless an operator explicitly asks for the old in-process arm, it runs on the stateless driver, whose state lives in a store rather than in one process's memory.

tour.title: One phase per claim
tour.say: A worker claims the run under a lease, loads its committed state, advances exactly one phase and commits, so a different process can carry on where the last one stopped.

tour.title: Only committed history
tour.say: Every phase appends to a journal, but only records at or below the committed watermark are ever replayed. A worker that died mid-write leaves orphans that get swept, never applied.

tour.title: Events through an outbox
tour.say: A phase records the events it wants shown instead of emitting them inline, so a phase that re-runs after a crash does not announce the same thing twice.

tour.title: No blind re-sends
tour.say: When a resumed run does not know whether a tool call landed, it adopts a recorded result, re-fires only retry-safe work, and otherwise asks the outward record before doing anything.

tour.title: Steer mid-run
tour.say: An owner's redirect is sealed into the run's steer inbox before it is acknowledged. The next decide phase claims it, and a committed receipt keeps the model from seeing it twice.

tour.title: Finish the announcement
tour.say: If a run ends but the process dies before the ending is broadcast, a background projector replays the recorded ending from the journal without rebuilding the run.

tour.title: Clear stuck parks
tour.say: Every thirty minutes a reconciler looks for runs parked past their deadline or waiting on children that have all finished, proves it, and retires them so nothing waits forever.

tour.title: Keep long-run context bounded
tour.say: Long runs retain a bounded recent conversation and an index of older results. Resumed decisions use the same window, with references for reading older evidence.

tour.title: Settle ambiguous interruptions safely
tour.say: An unowned ambiguous continuation is marked interrupted only after fresh checks. Saved work remains available for an explicit new attempt.

features.name: Verified coding completion
features.oneLine: Runs the project's required checks on the exact code a coding run produced, and sends failures back for repair.
features.maturityEvidence: Wired at boot from config (magician-bin/src/main.rs:9545-9551). Seed config sets verification.mode: observe (magician-config.yaml:396), which runs checks and records attestations but never holds completion; code default is Disabled (execution/verification/mod.rs:152-161). Enforce still needs an owner baseline, verification_state on task cards, and both coding engines activating together (docs/components/magician/verification-controller.md:508-520).

locations.why: Config mode with env kill switch

uiSurface.description: VibeDev project build settings, where the project checks verification runs are shown and customised

tour.title: Catch the success
tour.say: When a coding run reports success, the gate decides, before the task is marked done, whether that candidate success must be held for verification.

tour.title: Open a gate
tour.say: The task service opens a verification gate for the candidate. Under enforce the task stays visibly verifying; under observe, the shipped default, it completes as usual while evidence is still recorded.

tour.title: Decide what checked means
tour.say: The repository's own checks are merged with the owner's baseline, which a repository may add to but never remove. With no required checks, the run ends explicitly unverified rather than silently passing.

tour.title: Snapshot the exact code
tour.say: The controller captures a content-addressed snapshot of exactly the candidate code, and checks run in a disposable copy so build output cannot change what was verified.

tour.title: Run every check
tour.say: One shared runner executes the entire required policy against that snapshot, with per-check timeouts and a bounded tail of each command's output.

tour.title: Record the evidence
tour.say: Results go into an immutable attestation keyed to the snapshot and policy, so a snapshot that is already green is accepted again without rerunning anything.

tour.title: Bounded repair
tour.say: A failure hands normalised diagnostics back to the same engineer for another round, until the repair, time or spend budget runs out or the failures stop changing.

tour.title: Survive restarts
tour.say: A reconciler re-offers unsettled gates every minute by default, so a gate interrupted by a restart still reaches a verdict.

features.name: Run guardrails
features.oneLine: Detects loops, enforces spending and explicit run budgets, preserves progress through provider outages, and asks before critical steps.
features.maturityEvidence: The apply phase runs the loop check and criticality gate on every step (run_loop/phases/apply.rs:3092, 3348). Budget ceilings default to $100 native and harness (magician-config.yaml:2170-2172) and GET/POST /tasks/{task_id}/budget is mounted at magician-bin/src/main.rs:13302-13307, called from the /budget slash command (ui/unified-ui/src/lib/magician/chat/slashCommandActions.ts:133). Plan: docs/archive/plans/2026-10-03-slash-commands-and-run-budgets.md.

uiSurface.description: The /budget and /budget default slash commands in the chat composer

tour.title: Gate every step
tour.say: Before a step fires, the apply phase checks it against the run's loop history and its approval rules, so a repetitive or risky action is caught before anything happens.

tour.title: Spot loops
tour.say: The loop detector fingerprints the environment and each proposed action, flagging repeated states, back-and-forth cycles and actions that make no progress.

tour.title: Fingerprint the page
tour.say: Each observed browser page is hashed into a tree of structure and content, so comparing two root hashes tells whether anything actually changed.

tour.title: Ask before critical steps
tour.say: The model tags each action with a criticality hint, and an action marked critical becomes a confirmation request to the owner instead of running straight away.

tour.title: Check the budget
tour.say: At the top of each iteration the run re-reads its budget grants, recomputes its token and cost ceilings, and publishes a live snapshot that the budget endpoint reads.

tour.title: Owner raises the limit
tour.say: The owner can add spend, tokens, iterations or time with the budget command. At a run limit, an approval card offers an extension and continues the same run with its progress and usage retained.

tour.title: Keep what it saw
tour.say: Observation screenshots are stored under each execution, so the owner can later open exactly what the agent was looking at.

tour.title: Ride out a provider outage
tour.say: A provider outage retries with backoff without consuming productive iterations. After repeated failures, ordinary task runs pause for Retry or Cancel, keeping their checkpoint.

tour.title: Let long work continue
tour.say: Ordinary task runs have no fixed wall clock. Explicit budgets, inactivity checks and stuck-work detection still bound what they can do.

tour.title: Signal the final answer
tour.say: When work enters final synthesis, the task shows that it is writing the answer. Useful partial findings remain visible alongside any unresolved gaps.

features.name: Governed tool dispatch
features.oneLine: Every tool call an agent makes passes one policy, one catalog and one audited dispatch path, scoped to your workspace.
features.maturityEvidence: On the default execution path: the native catalog is the single source of truth for model-visible tools (agentic/native_catalog.rs:1-6), the invoker routes governed packages before the legacy CLI dispatcher (primitive_dispatch/capability_invoker.rs:398-403, 467), and boot installs the work-modules bridge (magician-bin/src/main.rs:11846). GET /agents/{id}/effective-tools (main.rs:12202) feeds the Crew page EffectiveToolPolicyPanel.

uiSurface.description: Crew page effective tool policy panel showing what each agent may call

tour.title: One policy per decision
tour.say: Before each model decision, one immutable tool-policy snapshot is resolved for the agent, and every tool list and permission check derives from it. A schema the model sees is never permission on its own.

tour.title: Build the tool list
tour.say: The native catalog turns that policy into the tools the model is offered: control tools such as yield and ask the user, delegation tools when there are targets, and skill capability tools.

tour.title: Ask the model
tour.say: The decision goes to the model through the provider adapter, with the run's history and that catalog, and the reply comes back as native tool calls.

tour.title: Lower the reply
tour.say: Lowering validates the tool calls and turns them into typed decisions, with every work tool going down one shared path as a pack action.

tour.title: Resolve per workspace
tour.say: The scoped resolver hands back a cached, immutable capability registry for this person and workspace, evicted whenever its skills change.

tour.title: Route the call
tour.say: Skills that ship a governed runtime package go to the governed runtime; older skills go to the template dispatcher, which runs one short-lived subprocess per call.

tour.title: Governed runtime
tour.say: The governed runtime selects and checks the credential profile and records an audit entry before running, and once chosen it never falls back to the legacy dispatcher.

tour.title: Scoped local bridges
tour.say: Some skills call back into Magician itself. The work-modules bridge mints a per-call, host-only token for that and revokes it as soon as the call ends.

features.name: Lean model context
features.oneLine: Keeps the model's context small: big tool results are stored and read by reference, and tools load only when selected.
features.maturityEvidence: agent_surface_runtime says the unified runtime and every surface are active by default, with working_set and result_projection limits (magician-config.yaml:1072-1091). Task runs project every action result (agentic/executor.rs:53206); chat and voice use the same projector (chat/service.rs:49938). POST /tasks/{id}/results/read is mounted under /api/magician/v3 (magician-bin/src/main.rs:14961).

uiSurface.description: Complete-result reader that pages stored tool results back into the web app

tour.title: A tool returns
tour.say: After a tool runs in a task, its redacted result goes to one shared lifecycle that chat and voice also use, owned by the task, the chat or the voice session.

tour.title: Store the whole result
tour.say: The complete result is stored once under its owner with a deterministic reference, so a retry or replay never stores it twice.

tour.title: Show a bounded view
tour.say: The projector builds a bounded view for the model without cutting a value in half, plus separate spoken and display summaries, and notes what was left out.

tour.title: Read more on demand
tour.say: The model gets a read result tool that pages through the stored result by reference, cursor and field paths, up to a thousand records at a time.

tour.title: Every read re-checked
tour.say: Each read re-checks the owner, the agent's current authority and the content hash, so a reference is only a locator and never a credential.

tour.title: Load tools on demand
tour.say: Tools follow the same idea: the model selects tool families by name, only authorised ones load, and past the limit the least recently used family is unloaded.

tour.title: Apps read it too
tour.say: The task API pages through the same stored results, so the web app can rebuild a complete result that the model only ever saw a slice of.

features.name: One boot, kept alive
features.oneLine: One supervisor starts the decision engine, Magicutor and Magician in order, and restarts any of them that crash.
features.maturityEvidence: make run-supervisor / run-all start it (Makefile:2834, 2863); defaults manage all three services with a 5-restarts-per-5-minutes budget and 10 s cooldown (magic-supervisor/src/main.rs:143-160); the health task restarts Magician after an unexpected exit (main.rs:1313); magician-bin serves a bootstrap listener and only releases background work once every HTTP worker is built (magician-bin/src/startup_http.rs:138, main.rs:15081). Documented in docs/components/magic-supervisor/supervisor.md.

locations.why: Watch the desktop without fighting Quit

tour.title: Supervisor wakes up
tour.say: The supervisor starts with the operating system signals already wired, so a stop during boot still shuts every child down cleanly.

tour.title: Start in order
tour.say: It starts the decision engine first, then Magicutor, then Magician two seconds later, and opens a small local control port for restart and status commands.

tour.title: Own process group
tour.say: Magician runs as the leader of its own process group, with its logs relayed line by line, so a stop can reach every helper it spawned.

tour.title: Plan the runtimes
tour.say: Inside Magician, the boot resolves a runtime plan from the scale profile and CPU count, then builds separate worker pools for requests, agent runs and vector search.

tour.title: Boot in order
tour.say: Before any store opens, it publishes pricing, budgets and the outward capture posture, installs storage, purges deleted workspaces, and opens a bootstrap listener so the UI can load early.

tour.title: Swap in the app
tour.say: When every route is built, the full application replaces the bootstrap one on the same socket. Only then are bots and heavy background jobs released.

tour.title: Watch and revive
tour.say: Every twenty seconds the supervisor checks health. If Magician exits on its own, it is restarted, while a deliberate stop is never fought.

tour.title: Bounded crash loops
tour.say: Restarts draw on a rolling budget of five in five minutes, so a crash loop backs off instead of spinning forever.

tour.title: Watch the desktop without fighting Quit
tour.say: The supervisor can relaunch the desktop app after a crash. A deliberate Quit is respected, and repeated crashes draw on a bounded restart budget.

features.name: Live updates everywhere
features.oneLine: Every run, chat and notice streams to open screens over one resumable socket, and is kept on disk so a refresh shows the same.
features.maturityEvidence: The broadcaster is built once at boot and the per-workspace log writer is spawned there (magician/src/magician_core/builder.rs:488); the socket is routed at /api/magician/v2/realtime/ws (magician-bin/src/main.rs:13560) and the UI's single EventHub owns it (ui/unified-ui/src/lib/realtime/eventHub.ts:1-25). Sequenced resume is documented in docs/components/unified-ui/event-hub.md and docs/components/magician/v2-websocket-events.md; make event-taxonomy-check gates every build (Makefile:1003).

locations.why: Separates active work from pending owner input for Chat presence

uiSurface.description: Every page shares one realtime connection that reconnects and resumes on its own; the Events page shows the full live stream with a day of backfill, and the same stream card sits inside the execution panel.

tour.title: One way in
tour.say: Every producer, from agent runs to chat, emits through the one broadcaster. Approval requests are committed to a durable journal before anyone can see them.

tour.title: Number every event
tour.say: The hub stamps each event with a rising sequence number and keeps the last eight thousand in a ring, so a reconnecting screen can ask for exactly what it missed.

tour.title: Open the socket
tour.say: A screen connects once. The server checks the origin and parameters, says hello with its epoch and sequence, and replays the gap if the client asked to resume.

tour.title: Scope and backpressure
tour.say: Only events visible to this workspace are forwarded. If the client falls behind, the socket stays open and sends a single resync instead of dropping the connection.

tour.title: The app listens
tour.say: In the browser, one hub dedupes frames by epoch and sequence and hands each event to the features subscribed to it, telling them to reload when a resync arrives.

tour.title: Route progress messages
tour.say: The progress router listens on the same bus, turns raw events into progress messages, journals them, and delivers them to chat, webhook and agent memory subscriptions.

tour.title: Taxonomy picks rendering
tour.say: The shared event taxonomy decides what each surface shows, so chat skips internal streaming noise while the operator stream keeps everything.

tour.title: Survive a refresh
tour.say: A writer appends every event to its workspace log and keeps a day or the last two thousand rows, so reloading a page shows what was live a moment ago.

tour.title: Working or Needs you
tour.say: Chat combines turn and task state for its presence sphere. A task paused for your answer shows Needs you, while an active response remains Working.

features.name: Storage with governance
features.oneLine: Data sits behind a leased, typed storage layer, and every database can be inspected, compacted and trimmed without losing a row.
features.maturityEvidence: magician-bin installs one StorageRuntime and acquires the default scope lease on every server boot (magician-bin/src/main.rs:1677-1679, 2165) and serves GET /health/storage (main.rs:12136); automatic DuckDB maintenance is on in the seed (magician-config.yaml:163-173) and spawned after readiness (main.rs:15082); the /storage page and its routes are live (magician-api/src/storage_governance_api.rs:78). Remote adapters stay dormant per docs/components/magician/storage-abstraction.md.

uiSurface.description: The Storage page lists every database, journal and folder with its size, safety class and policy, and offers confirmed actions: compact one or all databases, compact parquet partitions, apply retention, and clear metrics, while showing the automatic maintenance status.

tour.title: Install storage first
tour.say: Before any store opens, the boot checks that no newer build has claimed this data, opens the local storage runtime, and takes the lease on the default workspace.

tour.title: One writer only
tour.say: The lease is an exclusive file lock with a rising generation. A second Magician pointed at the same workspace is refused instead of corrupting it.

tour.title: Files stay truth
tour.say: Task and monitor lists read from a small index that can always be rebuilt from the files on disk, and a half-built index is never served.

tour.title: See everything stored
tour.say: The storage snapshot walks every database and folder in the workspace and labels each one, from authoritative truth to regenerable caches.

tour.title: Compact on request
tour.say: When the owner confirms, each chosen database, such as analytics, channel assist or the thread list, is compacted by its own store, one at a time.

tour.title: Prove, then swap
tour.say: The database is copied fresh, its tables, indexes and row counts are fingerprinted and compared, and only then swapped in, with a backup to roll back if anything differs.

tour.title: Maintenance on schedule
tour.say: After startup, a background loop checks channel assist and feed databases in every workspace and compacts the fragmented ones, respecting a cooldown.

features.name: Stays light under load
features.oneLine: Caps how many agents run at once, nests delegation without deadlock, and closes idle workspace databases so memory stays bounded.
features.maturityEvidence: Limits come from runtime.scale (magician-config.yaml:6-30) and are applied before the runtimes exist (magician-bin/src/main.rs:1450); every top-level run is admitted (execution/agentic/executor.rs:41887); the idle reaper runs as a supervised task (main.rs:11671); idle caches are in CHANGELOG [Unreleased] (magician/CHANGELOG.md:20). Open follow-ups: the RSS tripwire is measured but never configured, so it never rejects (magician/src/magician_v2/local_resource_governor.rs:1-9), and harness-root permits are a compile-time constant (magician-core/src/local_resource_governor.rs:15-27).

uiSurface.description: Runtime, Resources shows live gauges for active agent loops, queued triggers, event backlog, lock waits and search load, each with a watch or pressure severity and advice.

tour.title: Size the host
tour.say: At boot a scale profile, from small four-core machines to large cloud hosts, decides thread counts, the live-agent cap and delegation width, with config overrides on top.

tour.title: Ask to run
tour.say: Every top-level agent run asks the governor for a slot before it starts. Nested work inside an admitted run does not count twice.

tour.title: Three gates
tour.say: The governor checks the memory tripwire, then the per-agent cap of eight open runs, then the global cap of fifty, and rejects cleanly rather than overloading the machine.

tour.title: Delegation without deadlock
tour.say: Delegated children draw from a separate pool for each nesting level, so parents waiting on grandchildren can never hold the slots those grandchildren need.

tour.title: No startup stampede
tour.say: Heavy first passes, like reconciling subscriptions or materializing the feed, wait until the server is ready and then run one at a time instead of all at once.

tour.title: Close what sleeps
tour.say: Workspace databases unused for a minute are closed, and at most eight idle ones are kept. Anything still mid-query stays pinned, and no data is ever deleted.

tour.title: Watch the gauges
tour.say: A snapshot of every counter and high-water mark feeds the Resources page, so an operator can see pressure building before anything is rejected.

features.name: Guided setup wizard
features.oneLine: Asks what you want Magician to do, then installs, starts and checks the whole stack from source, and only calls a step done when a probe agrees.
features.maturityEvidence: Since 5f8e55f03 (2026-10-15) the macOS source path runs end to end: the wizard, `make install-source` (which `make install` uses for dev/local on macOS) and Desktop's 'Install native services here' all run scripts/install-source-checkout.sh in three stages (prepare, start, verify). It installs required software and the local memory model, builds with `make build-source-debug`, installs a checked native package, starts the per-user LaunchAgent ai.magicbeans.magican.backend, and waits for core readiness with install-verify.sh --core. Package-only and container terminal paths stay disabled with reasons, and full installation validation is still in progress (docs/components/magician-setup/README.md, docs/quickstart.md).

locations.why: One install contract for terminal and Desktop
Fills both env files, never replaces
Desktop builds from the checkout too
Same installer, logged to the data folder

tour.title: Start the wizard
tour.say: The wizard starts in the terminal. It can just report status, rehearse a dry run, or simulate other machines, and otherwise asks what you want Magician to do.

tour.title: From wishes to parts
tour.say: Your chosen capabilities are turned into the components they need from the shared component graph, and the plan is shown before anything is installed.

tour.title: One installer, three doors
tour.say: Once you accept the plan, the wizard runs the same source installer as make install and the desktop app. It installs the software Magician needs, builds it once, and installs a checked package in its own folder, apart from your data.

tour.title: Prepare, start, verify
tour.say: Every door shares one contract with three stages. Prepare builds and installs, start runs the backend as a login service, and verify waits until Magician, Magicutor, Pi, the memory model and the desktop gateway all answer.

tour.title: Check before acting
tour.say: For each component it asks whether this machine can run it, whether its dependencies work, and whether it is already there, so a re-run stays quiet.

tour.title: Probe is the authority
tour.say: A step counts as done only when its probe sees the thing working. A command that merely exited cleanly is not enough.

tour.title: Keys, written safely
tour.say: Pasted keys go into both runtime env files with owner-only permissions. A key that is already set is never replaced, and an empty placeholder is filled where it stands.

tour.title: Wait for people
tour.say: For steps only a person can do, like granting a permission in System Settings, it keeps probing until the change shows up. The desktop app confirms the grant, so a click on done is never enough on its own.

tour.title: Done means ready
tour.say: At the end it looks again at everything you chose. If a capability or a required service is not ready, setup says which ones and exits with an error instead of a cheerful finish.

tour.title: Or from the desktop app
tour.say: In the desktop app, Install native services here runs the same installer from a source checkout, shows progress with a log in the data folder, and waits for the same readiness checks before it opens onboarding.

features.name: Sandboxed shell and network
features.oneLine: Runs every agent shell command in an OS box: secret files hidden, nested agent CLIs blocked, public internet only via a proxy.
features.maturityEvidence: On in the seed: execution.network_policy.mode is public (magician-config.yaml:2185-2187) and shell_sandbox.os_enforce is true (magician-config.yaml:2200), though the code defaults are off (NetworkMode::Allow at magician/src/config.rs:2254-2258; os_enforce false at runtime-core/src/runtime.rs:80). Published at boot (magician/src/magician_core/builder.rs:854) and on live reload (magician-api/src/web_api.rs:18846). Listed under [Unreleased] in magician/CHANGELOG.md:15-16; design in docs/archive/plans/2026-10-13-hard-shell-sandbox-design.md. Open follow-up: on Linux the public mode is not enforced because bwrap's new network namespace cannot reach the host proxy (shell_box.rs:18-21).

locations.why: Decides boxed, refused or god mode
Wraps command in sandbox-exec or bwrap
HTTP tool policy and god mode

tour.title: A shell command arrives
tour.say: An agent asks to run a shell command. The string checks run first, then the runtime decides whether the command goes into the operating system box, or to god mode for the owner's approval.

tour.title: Wrap in a box
tour.say: Outside coding runs, the command is wrapped in sandbox exec on a Mac or bubblewrap on Linux, so the kernel enforces the rules however the command is phrased.

tour.title: Plan what is allowed
tour.say: The plan lets the command write only under its working folders, temp and tool caches. SSH keys, cloud credentials, the runtime env files and the vault stay unreadable.

tour.title: No nested agents
tour.say: The profile also refuses to start other agent command line tools like claude or codex, which would carry their own credentials past every Magician gate. Network is allowed only to the proxy port.

tour.title: Through the egress proxy
tour.say: In public mode the child's proxy variables point at a localhost proxy. It reads each CONNECT or plain HTTP request and refuses with a clear reason when the destination is blocked.

tour.title: Vet every address
tour.say: The proxy resolves the host itself and requires every address to be public, so loopback, private networks and cloud metadata stay out of reach and a DNS answer cannot rebind.

tour.title: Same rule for HTTP
tour.say: The built in HTTP tool follows the same policy through a filtering resolver, redirects included. In god mode a blocked host becomes an approval card instead of a failure.

features.name: Connect any MCP server
features.oneLine: Calls MCP tools under policy, using scoped OAuth when an account is required.
features.maturityEvidence: Governed stdio and Streamable HTTP dispatch support scoped OAuth or explicitly anonymous contracts. Official Metabase, Shopify, Swiggy Scenes, Zepto and Zomato packages ship. mcp_commerce.rs binds approved cart quotes and single-use claims; Shopify hands off checkout links. Zomato checkout remains unqualified. Product-side resume of input-required/task outcomes remains a follow-up.

uiSurface.description: A pending sign-in appears as a 'Finish signing in' card in the HITL attention surfaces; the desktop onboarding opens the provider page for a skill's MCP sign-in.

tour.title: Start a sign-in
tour.say: The owner connects an MCP skill, like Metabase or a grocery store. Setup asks the engine to begin sign-in for that skill's exact server and issuer.

tour.title: SDK does the protocol
tour.say: The official MCP SDK handles discovery, client registration and PKCE. The coordinator binds the result to one profile and produces a browser link that cannot be printed or serialized.

tour.title: Survive a restart
tour.say: A pending record goes into the encrypted vault, so if Magician restarts mid sign-in, the browser callback can still finish the exchange.

tour.title: The callback returns
tour.say: The provider redirects back to an opaque callback path. The broker matches it to the live flow, or to the restored coordinator, and each callback works only once.

tour.title: Agent calls a tool
tour.say: Later an agent uses the skill. The runtime fetches a fresh bearer token, connects, discovers the tools and filters them through the skill's own catalog policy.

tour.title: A bounded call
tour.say: Only discovered tools can be called, arguments are size checked, and a continuation slot is reserved in case the server asks for more input or starts a long task.

tour.title: Never double submit
tour.say: A finished result goes back to the agent. An unfinished one is reported as possibly accepted with a note not to retry, so a checkout is never placed twice.

tour.title: Choose local or remote transport
tour.say: Governed MCP tools can run over local standard input and output or remote HTTP. Anonymous servers need no login; account tools keep workspace-scoped credentials.

tour.title: Discover the official Metabase tools
tour.say: Metabase uses its official MCP service. Discover the current tool schemas, prefer bounded reads, and obtain approval before changing shared content or data.

tour.title: Review commerce before checkout
tour.say: Shopify hands off checkout links, while supported Swiggy checkout uses a short-lived cart quote and single-use claim. Zomato checkout remains unqualified.

features.name: Sign-in and workspaces
features.oneLine: Owner signs in by password, Google or GitHub, mints API tokens, and every request is pinned to a workspace they own.
features.maturityEvidence: The auth middleware wraps the whole /api/magician/v2 scope and auth routes are mounted there (magician-bin/src/main.rs:12150-12155). Seed auth.mode is open with allow_signup (magician-config.yaml:2361-2364), but open mode is bootstrap only: once any identity exists a bearer is required (middleware.rs:298-321). A /login page exists (ui/unified-ui/src/routes/login/+page.svelte); social providers need a client_id, commented out in the seed (magician-config.yaml:2367-2371). Docs: docs/components/magician/auth.md.

uiSurface.description: The /login page takes a username and password (the first one creates the owner) and offers social sign-in when providers are configured.

tour.title: Sign in
tour.say: The owner types a username and password on the login page.

tour.title: Throttle, then verify
tour.say: A sliding window throttle turns away repeated guesses before any password hashing. On a fresh install, the first login creates the owner and adopts the existing anonymous data.

tour.title: Mint a session
tour.say: A random session token is shown once and stored only as a hash, so reading the files on disk never yields a working credential.

tour.title: Every request checked
tour.say: Each API request passes this gate. It resolves the bearer, accepts bot and session tokens, refuses terminal grants, and after the first identity exists, refuses requests with no bearer at all.

tour.title: Pin the workspace
tour.say: The principal comes from the verified session. A requested workspace is accepted only if the registry says this person owns it, so a caller cannot name someone else's scope.

tour.title: Ownership registry
tour.say: Workspaces are created explicitly and recorded per person. Deleted ones are tombstoned, and their bots lose their credentials on the next call.

features.name: Auto-read verification codes
features.oneLine: When an agent needs a login code, Magician reads it from the inboxes or phone you allowed and answers the ask for you.
features.maturityEvidence: On by default: HitlVerificationCodesSettings.enabled defaults to true (magician/src/config.rs:5620-5643) and the seed sets hitl.verification_codes.enabled: true (magician-config.yaml:2561-2569). Wired at boot with Gmail, AgentMail, Messages and Android watches (magician-bin/src/main.rs:7605-7653); routes at main.rs:1065-1068, 12379-12382 and 13932-13936; per-account grant checkbox on the Observe page. Docs: docs/components/magician/verification-code-retrieval.md.

uiSurface.description: On the Observe page each Gmail, AgentMail or iMessage account has a separate 'verification codes' checkbox; the device pairing panel lists which paired phones may read codes.

tour.title: Grant one inbox
tour.say: The owner ticks a separate box on one observed account. Observing an inbox alone never grants the right to read login codes from it.

tour.title: Agent needs a code
tour.say: When a run raises an ask whose published spec is a one time code, the resolver picks it up from the HITL event stream. When the ask resolves, it stops.

tour.title: Start the watchers
tour.say: It looks up which sources this workspace permitted right now, and starts one bounded watcher per source, such as Gmail, AgentMail, Messages or the Android companion.

tour.title: Poll with limits
tour.say: Each watcher polls until the deadline or a poll cap, re-checks the permission before every fetch, and gives up after repeated failures.

tour.title: Trust facts only
tour.say: A message counts only if its receive time, account and sender domain match the challenge. Display names and anything the message says about itself are ignored.

tour.title: Pull the code
tour.say: The code is a four to eight digit run next to a verification cue. Links are cut out first, and two different candidates mean the person decides.

tour.title: Answer the ask
tour.say: The code answers the ask through the same first response wins door a person uses, so the model sees only a status, never the code.

features.name: Agent spend budgets
features.oneLine: Set model spending and action limits, follow usage in a shared ledger, and pause autonomous work when its spending window is exhausted.
features.maturityEvidence: Off in code (ResourceAuthorityConfig.enabled has #[serde(default)], resource_authority/config.rs:19-26) but on in the seed with daily caps: 50 email sends, 50 WhatsApp sends, 2000 INR each for zepto-mcp and swiggy-mcp (magician-config.yaml:2635-2686). The disk-backed resolver is built at boot (magician-bin/src/main.rs:7006), routes mounted under /api/magician/v2 (main.rs:13491), and the /budget page manages ceilings and tokens. Docs: docs/components/magician/resource-authority-api.md.

locations.why: Park autonomous work at the limit
Post counted model costs to the ledger

uiSurface.description: The Budget page lists system ceilings and spend tokens, edits ceilings, revokes tokens, shows the ledger and reservations, and can freeze all spending.

tour.title: Budgets in config
tour.say: Budgets are rows in the config: a scope, a commodity such as email sends or rupees, a ceiling and a period. The seed caps email and WhatsApp sends at fifty a day.

tour.title: A costly tool runs
tour.say: When an agent calls a tool that declares a cost, dispatch asks for a reservation first. The tool runs only if it is admitted, and the hold is committed or rolled back afterwards.

tour.title: One door for spend
tour.say: Chat dispatch, MCP checkout and the REST API all go through this one function. It finds the matching budgets and decides what happens when none exists.

tour.title: Budgets become tokens
tour.say: On first use each matching row turns into a spend token for the person, agent or tool, so several budgets can stack on one call.

tour.title: The hard gate
tour.say: The gate checks the system freeze first, then token status, expiry, balance, every system ceiling, the period ceiling and velocity limits, and only then records a reservation.

tour.title: Written to disk
tour.say: Each workspace keeps its own ledger and tokens on disk, written off the async threads with fsync so a crash cannot leave them inconsistent.

tour.title: Recover after a crash
tour.say: On load, reservations with no matching commit or rollback are rebuilt, so money held before a crash is still accounted for.

tour.title: Pull the brake
tour.say: Settings brings model spending and action limits together. The owner can change ceilings, add to the current window, revoke tokens or freeze action spending.

tour.title: One model spending envelope
tour.say: A shared envelope counts model, decision, coding and voice costs. The owner sets window, lifetime and per-run limits, with explicit unlimited choices.

tour.title: Park autonomous work at the limit
tour.say: Exhausted autonomous work parks until its window resets or the owner adds spending room. Foreground requests remain reachable and still count toward usage.

tour.title: Post counted model costs to the ledger
tour.say: Counted model costs are periodically posted to each workspace’s resource ledger. Model limits live beside action limits without charging the same call twice.

features.name: Artifact lifecycle
features.oneLine: A catalog and policy engine that decide when task outputs go stale, expire or get swept, built but not switched on yet.
features.maturityEvidence: Built and tested but not wired: LifecycleService (artifacts/service.rs:84) is only constructed in tests (pipeline/artifact.rs:1100-1119), and PipelineOrchestrator::set_lifecycle_service (pipeline/orchestrator.rs:362) has no caller; LifecycleScheduler, SanitizationGateway and FileCatalog are likewise only built in their own tests. The live path today is artifacts/durable_store.rs.

tour.title: One catalog
tour.say: Every task output would be registered in one catalog with its scope, freshness, references and sensitivity, while the bytes stay where they are.

tour.title: Five layers decide
tour.say: A policy engine decides whether an output is fresh, stale or expired. Legal holds win over per-item protection, which wins over domain defaults.

tour.title: Mark, then sweep
tour.say: A sweeper first marks candidates with a reason for each, then deletes a bounded number per run, never touching anything protected or still referenced.

tour.title: Safe views only
tour.say: Readers get a projection instead of the raw output, with secrets and sensitive paths stripped for that surface.

tour.title: Not switched on
tour.say: All of this is built and tested, but nothing in the running server creates the service yet. Today outputs live in the durable store.

features.name: Reach it from anywhere, safely
features.oneLine: Phones, the ESP32 and remote desktops reach your Magician through your own Cloudflare tunnel, behind Access, with a per-device key on top.
features.maturityEvidence: Provisioned by scripts: ensure-machine-tunnel.sh (one tunnel per machine), ensure-connect-access.sh (service-token Access app on connect.<zone> plus the narrow enrollment bypass), ensure-ui-access.sh (email-login Access on ui.<zone>) and ensure-magician-tunnel.sh (public webhook host). The server verifies the Access JWT when MAGICIAN_CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN and MAGICIAN_CF_ACCESS_AUD are set; MAGICIAN_CF_ACCESS_MODE=require rejects requests without one, while the default verify mode checks any assertion it sees. Device identity always comes from the pairing record. docs/components/scripts/README.md and docs/setup/mobile.md.

uiSurface.description: Desktop Settings chooses which backend connect.<zone> reaches (native, container or a remote server) and shows each one's health; the phone apps keep one profile per paired machine and switch between them.

tour.title: One tunnel per machine
tour.say: Each Mac gets its own Cloudflare tunnel and its own hostnames, because a shared tunnel lets Cloudflare send a request to whichever machine it picks. Your phone keeps one connection profile per paired machine and switches between them.

tour.title: One address, split by path
tour.say: When a phone pairs, it learns one address: connect dot your domain. The tunnel splits it by path. Host calls go to this Mac's desktop app, and the API goes to whichever Magician backend you chose.
tour.evidence: connect.<zone>: /host/* -> 127.0.0.1:3017; /health and /api/* -> :3002, :13002 or a remote HTTPS origin (scripts/select-connect-backend.sh)

tour.title: Switch without re-pairing
tour.say: Moving between the native backend, a container and a remote server rewrites just those two routes through the Cloudflare API, and only after the new backend passes a health check. The address never changes, so no phone has to pair again.
tour.evidence: ensure_healthy refuses an unhealthy target; the change is read back and verified

tour.title: Two keys to get in
tour.say: Every request from a phone carries two keys. A shared Cloudflare service token gets it past Access, and its own revocable device token tells Magician which device it is and whose data it may see.
tour.evidence: CF-Access-Client-Id / CF-Access-Client-Secret plus X-Magician-Device-Id and a device bearer (scripts/ensure-connect-access.sh)

tour.title: The one door around Access
tour.say: Only the one-time pairing exchange skips Access. It still needs the random secret from the pairing code, which expires in five minutes and works once, and it is how a confirmed phone receives both of its keys.
tour.evidence: DEVICE_ENROLLMENT_TTL_MS = 5 min; 256-bit secret, stored as a digest; Access bypass covers only the exact exchange paths

tour.title: Check the edge, trust only Magician
tour.say: Behind the tunnel, Magician checks Cloudflare's signed token against your account's published keys, so a forged header gets nowhere. Who you are still comes only from Magician's own device or session token; the shared service token is never treated as a person.
tour.evidence: Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion, RS256 with the team's keys; MAGICIAN_CF_ACCESS_MODE=require rejects requests without one

tour.title: The Mac as a remote engine's edge
tour.say: When Magician runs on a remote server, the Mac's desktop app pairs with it once, then dials out over a secure websocket, adding Access headers when the server sits behind Access. Nothing listens on the Mac.
tour.evidence: wss://<engine>/api/magician/v2/edge/bridge; desktop-only token in the OS keychain

tour.title: Your Mac, lent with limits
tour.say: The server admits that socket only for a paired desktop, then borrows the Mac's screen control, browser and read-only iMessage through it. The desktop refuses any call it did not offer.

tour.title: Webhooks stay public, but signed
tour.say: Webhook addresses stay outside Access, because WhatsApp and email providers can't log in. Instead a WhatsApp callback must carry a valid signature over its exact bytes, while the developer UI sits behind an email login.
tour.evidence: webhook.<zone> is never behind Access (scripts/ensure-magician-tunnel.sh); ui.<zone> uses an interactive email policy (scripts/ensure-ui-access.sh)

uiSurface.description: Browser choice, pairing and submission approvals use the shared owner question surfaces.

tour.title: Choose the paired browser
tour.say: Several extension browsers can be paired at once. An attended run lets the owner choose which signed-in browser should handle that work.

tour.title: Respect the agent’s transport grant
tour.say: The agent’s definition controls whether it may use a signed-in extension browser or only headed and headless contexts. Choosing a browser never widens that grant.

tour.title: Lease a window to the launch
tour.say: Concurrent launches receive separate window leases. Runs belonging to the same launch can share its window without closing another launch’s browser.

tour.title: Name the tab group
tour.say: A browser run sends a name for its tab group on first connect: the conversation’s title for a chat launch, otherwise the task’s title. The same name replaces “this task” on the which-browser card, and the first new tab reuses the untouched start page instead of leaving an empty one.

tour.title: Optionally hold final submissions
tour.say: With submission review enabled, a detected final form action waits for approval. The owner can approve once, permit that site, or deny.

tour.title: Keep site grants revocable
tour.say: A site approval remains visible and revocable. Dispatch checks the approved page and action again, while ordinary tool and outward-action checks still apply.

features.name: Long chats that keep their context
features.oneLine: When a conversation outgrows the model’s window, older turns are folded into a running summary for the model while the full transcript stays intact and searchable.
features.maturityEvidence: magician-config.yaml llm.chat_history.enabled: true (seed default); operation chat_history_compaction is mapped in llm-router.yaml; magician/src/config.rs validates the section at startup. Checkpoints are a disposable view: they never replace transcript entries, authorize tools, or replay completed effects.

uiSurface.description: Invisible in the composer: long chats keep answering with earlier context, and the model can search the full history when a detail was folded away.

tour.title: Know when to fold
tour.say: Past a share of the model’s budget, older history is folded in the background so the in-turn trigger rarely has work left. The most recent turns are always kept verbatim.

tour.title: Summarize, don’t replace
tour.say: A summarizer call maintains a factual handoff of the old turns, sized to the routed model’s own input window. Long tool output is cut to its head and tail for the summary; the full text stays in the transcript.

tour.title: A disposable view
tour.say: The checkpoint records which transcript prefix it covers. It never rewrites entries, grants tools, or replays finished effects, so dropping it loses nothing.

tour.title: Recall what was folded
tour.say: When the model needs a detail the summary dropped, a read-only history search looks it up in the complete transcript of the current session.
